jobs.title: Full Stack Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Company Overview

WarpWare is opening space for all through software innovation. Space accessibility is our highest priority in everything we do. Since our creation, we have become one of Denver’s most innovative space startups, specializing in helping spacecraft get to space fast.

Role Summary

WarpWare is seeking a Full Stack Application Software Engineer to develop capabilities for the WarpWare software platform, perform research and development, and deliver on contracts for a variety of commercial and government customers. Successful candidates will demonstrate a high degree of ownership, independence, and problem solving skills regardless of experience.

Application Process

Interested candidates should reach out via email to hiring@warpware.co. Due to a high volume of applications, WarpWare cannot guarantee candidates who apply only via LinkedIn will be considered.

Responsibilities

This role drives the development, scaling, and support of the WarpWare app, the unified mission software platform that space companies use to accelerate development from concept to launch. WarpWare replaces fragmented, custom-build software by providing a single, continuous, unified foundation used across launch vehicles, satellites rendezvous, low-Earth orbit, and cislunar operations. Bridging the gap between advanced software engineering and real-world space missions, the position owns everything from local application code deployed on customer environments to the cloud infrastructure and automated release pipelines that keep the platform robust.
Design, develop, and test the WarpWare application deployed locally on customer computers
Build and maintain the cloud infrastructure that supports the WarpWare application
Own and improve the build, test, and release pipeline that keeps the application robust
Interface regularly with customers to support deployments and gather feedback
Apply systems engineering principles to the development, analysis, and execution of complex systems
Think creatively to develop innovative solutions to challenging problems
Diagnose issues across customer environments, develop insights, and iterate on design to improve reliability and user experience
Develop software in C++, C#, type script, java script, and python, working across frontend, backend, and infrastructure code
Shape the future of the WarpWare platform

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related field
Demonstrated experience exercising strong ownership of complex problems
Willingness to challenge others and be challenged
Strong interpersonal and written communication skills
Strong coding and problem solving skills
Must be eligible to perform EAR / ITAR work

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing and deploying desktop or locally installed applications across multiple OS’s (e.g., linux, windows, macOS)
Experience with cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS, Azure, or GCP) and infrastructure as code
Experience building CI/CD pipelines and automated testing
Experience using C++, C#, type script, java script, and python
Experience working on space software projects
Experience with user interface design and delivery

Compensation & Benefits

SALARY: $90,000 - $150,000

HEALTHCARE: Company subsidized health, dental, and vision insurance

BENEFITS: WarpWare equity ownership, 401(K), flexible PTO

WarpWare is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected status.

jobs.title: QA Automation Engineer II
jobs.description:
7-Eleven is an iconic family of brands with over 86,000 locations, surpassing every retailer in the world. We revolutionize convenience, restaurants and fuel through cutting edge innovation — working hard to be the customer's first choice. 7-Eleven empowers our employees to "activate awesome" and make a meaningful impact in their stores and communities every day. If you're ready to grow, lead and make a difference, come join our team and help shape the future of convenience.

Job Description

7-Eleven is seeking a QA Automation Engineer II to help deliver reliable digital experiences. This role combines manual and automated testing throughout the Software Testing Life Cycle (STLC), from test planning through release reporting. You will work closely with developers and product managers to identify quality risks, investigate defects, and improve test coverage and automation.

What You’ll Do

Develop, execute, and improve automation frameworks and test scripts to increase testing efficiency, accuracy, and speed.
Define test objectives, plans, and strategies based on project requirements and schedules.
Participate in testing early in the development process to identify issues before they become more costly to fix.
Design, execute, and document manual, exploratory, and automated tests across application programming interfaces (APIs), web, and mobile applications.
Perform functional, progression, and regression testing; document and communicate defects clearly.
Analyze defects and investigate root causes using available application logs and database information.
Record and track defects in Jira, partnering with developers and product managers through resolution.
Debug issues and help identify corrective actions that support the quality of 7-Eleven apps.
Prepare test summary reports for releases and share results with relevant stakeholders.
Contribute to quality assurance practices across the STLC and to continuous improvement of testing activities.

What You’ll Bring

Bachelor’s degree.
At least 3 years of professional experience in software quality assurance or software testing.
Hands-on experience with both manual and automated testing across the STLC.
Experience planning tests and executing functional, progression, regression, and exploratory testing.
Experience testing APIs, web applications, and mobile applications.
Experience creating or working with test automation frameworks and scripts.
Ability to analyze defects and use logs and database information to investigate issues.
Experience documenting and tracking defects in Jira or a similar issue-tracking tool.
Clear written communication and the ability to work effectively with developers, product managers, and other stakeholders.
Position is onsite and based in Irving TX.

jobs.title: Scientific Software Engineer - Meteorological Decoders  for Observation Processing and Integration
jobs.description:
Lynker is seeking a highly skilled Software Engineer to support the NOAA/NWS Office of Modeling and Development by managing, developing, and optimizing the meteorological data decoder systems. This role focuses on the critical pipeline that converts diverse, native-format meteorological observations into standardized formats required for downstream numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems.

Duties of the Scientific Software Engineer will include the following

Technical Operations & R&D

Develop, maintain, and optimize C and Fortran programs used to decode raw meteorological bulletins.
Translate non-standard native data formats into BUFR and JEDI IODA netcdf by engineering specialized decoder logic
Ensure uninterrupted, efficient data flow by managing input and output streams for ingest data queues, descriptor lists, and temporary BUFR message storage.

Systems & Data Integration

Monitor and troubleshoot operational data ingestion across major meteorological data servers, including LDM, DBNet, GTS, and WIS2.
Ensure decoded data tanks are optimized for rapid assimilation into the NCEP NWP system, supporting the generation of thousands of daily weather products.
Manage and maintain the software repositories pertaining to legacy and operational decoder processing.

Coordination & Reporting

Liaise with upstream data originators and downstream NCO Operations users to seamlessly integrate new observational data types into the BUFR pipeline.
Report on software task progress, system performance metrics, and project risks to the Lead Scientist and Federal oversight managers.
Participate in the Modernization of Observation Infrastructure project (GEODE) to transition legacy decoder frameworks to modern architectures.

The Scientist Software Engineer selected for this role should meet the following qualifications

Advanced skills and knowledge of Fortran and C programming languages specifically tailored for data parsing and processing.
Deep understanding of BUFR (Binary Universal Form for the Representation of meteorological data), including table-driven descriptors and binary extraction logic.
Experience working in a UNIX/Linux environment with advanced shell scripting languages.
Demonstrated knowledge of meteorological data servers and distribution networks (LDM, DBNet, GTS, WIS2).
Skills and knowledge of High-Performance Computing (HPC) file systems and job schedulers (e.g., WCOSS environment, MPI, Slurm, LSF).
Knowledge of modern software development practices and version control software, particularly Git/GitHub/Gitflow.
Ability to perform complex, mission-critical debugging in a fast-paced, operational environment.

Additional desirable experiences and skills include

Knowledge of global Data Assimilation (DA) systems and observation networks.
Experience transitioning legacy meteorological codebases into Cloud environments.
Background in atmospheric physics or earth system modeling.

About Lynker

Lynker is a growing, employee owned business, specializing in professional, scientific and technical services. Our continually expanding team combines scientific expertise with mature, results-driven processes and tools to achieve technically sound, cost effective solutions in hydrology/water sciences, geospatial analysis, information technology, resource management, conservation, and management and business process improvement.

We focus on putting the right people in the right place to be effective. And having the right people is critical for success. Our streamlined organization enables and empowers our talented professionals to tackle our customers' scientific and technical priorities - creatively and effectively.

Lynker offers a team-oriented work environment, and the opportunity to work in a culture of exceptionally skilled professionals who embrace sound science and creative solutions. Lynker's benefits include the following

Comprehensive healthcare for the employee at no monthly cost
Healthcare benefit covers medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision
Personal Time Off (PTO) Policy plus paid holidays
Highly competitive compensation plan regularly calibrated against industry and location benchmarks
401(k) retirement plan with company-matching
Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) - we're all company owners!
Flexible spending accounts
Employee assistance program (EAP)
Short- and long-term disability insurance
Life and accident insurance
Tuition assistance/Training/Workforce improvement reimbursement per year
Spot bonuses for exceptional performance
Annual Employee Recognition Awards with bonuses
Employee Referral Program
Free centralized, self-directed Learning Management System to learn at your own pace
Personalized career growth plans for every employee

Lynker is an E-Verify employer.

Lynker is an equal opportunity employer and makes all employment decisions based on merit, qualifications, and business needs. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, or any other legally protected status under federal, state, or local laws
